speaker: Other
text: Well, thank you for having me. I apologize. I can't see everybody in person through the Zoom link. I don't know. That must be our IT department on our side making our computers too secure to interact. So, thank you for having me. My name is, as Ken Pruser said, I'm a district supervisor with USDA Wildlife Services. I was born and raised in Columbia County. I've been working as a wildlife biologist for the past 27 years, resolving Canada goose issues is one of my duties throughout the Hudson Valley. I cover New York State DEC regions 3, 4, and 5, which extends from Westchester, southern county border, up to Canada, out to Binghamton. We have a pretty large presence in the area. I made a site visit to Pine Plains last summer to look at the goose problem that was present there. So, to give everybody a background, on resident Canada geese, there are different species of Canada geese. What we're dealing with at Stissing Lake or the Pine Plains is resident Canada geese. These geese nest below the 40th parallel, and they do not migrate like their counterparts that nest in Canada and come down here and spend the winter. So, the population goal set by New York State DEC is a social caring capacity is about 85,000 birds. So, currently, New York State DEC estimates the population at 230,000 birds. So, there's an overabundance of Canada geese, which creates problems with variety issues mainly associated with their droppings. One Canada goose is estimated about a pound of droppings per day, or 90 individual droppings. When I was present at the lake, there was about 75 to 100 birds there, so you can see how that would add up very quickly as far as the damage that is there. So, I reviewed some of the techniques which are used to manage resident Canada geese. Obviously, some techniques won't work in your situation due to it's a beach and there's a public area there, so you couldn't fence off the area. They would deny access to the water. The other actions that were considered was a hazing program or harassment, but due to the size of Sissing Lake, if those birds were harassed with pyrotechnics, remote controlled boat or dog harassment, it would take an extensive effort to move the birds from the lake itself without pushing out to neighboring properties and causing the same damage. The geese themselves would only, studies have shown here in New York that when a goose is harassed intensely, the resident Canada geese will go about three miles and continue to return to the site through banding data. So, that leads us to what can we do to control the population? So, there's a couple of different ways to do that. Egg and nest treatment is one where you go out and locate the eggs and nests that are nesting along the lake and treat the eggs with 100% corn oil. That prevents the geese from hatching, the eggs from hatching, therefore minimizing the number of geese. However, by doing that, it's a long process, it would take over 15 years to do that due to the nature of the geese, these geese would lay, a female goose lays up to 50 eggs in her lifetime and they live up to access to 20 years sometimes. The other option that would not be feasible, I don't think, for there would be to allow the use of shooting to reduce the population to reinforce hazing, that's just due to the nature of Sissing Lake and the surrounding houses that would be there. So, the other population, the other recommendations that we talked about was a roundup and removal of the birds during the molt. Geese lose their primary flight feathers during the molt, so they cannot fly from about June 15th to July 15th. The birds are then captured in a corral pen somewhere on land, they're pushed off the water and into a pen, they're loaded alive in the poultry crates and are taken to a licensed poultry processing facility and then they're donated to the food bank. So those are the options that were reviewed. I would recommend a combination of efforts between egg and nest treatment and removal during the molt of the birds that are present there. So, I know I said a lot in a short amount of time, I apologize for talking too fast as I typically do, but if anybody has any questions or wants to talk about any of the methods that I talked about, I'd be more than happy to talk about it.
